title: Self-Service Infrastructure Catalog - Architecture Specification
description: Technology-agnostic architecture specification focusing on WHAT the system does, not HOW it's implemented

businessContext.purpose: Enable teams to provision, manage, and delete infrastructure through a self-service interface
businessContext.scope: Infrastructure lifecycle management from request to decommissioning

infrastructureManagement.description: Manage infrastructure lifecycle from provisioning to deletion

capabilities.name: Custom Infrastructure Provisioning
capabilities.description: Build infrastructure by composing reusable modules
businessRules: Project names must be unique within environment
All provisioning requires approval number (JIRA/CR)
Project age must be specified for lifecycle management

capabilities.name: Template-Based Provisioning
businessRules: Templates must exist in catalog before deployment
Template parameters are pre-validated

capabilities.name: Infrastructure Deletion
capabilities.description: Safely remove infrastructure with approval workflow
businessRules: Deletion requires approval via pull request
Metadata is archived before deletion
All dependent resources must be identified

capabilities.name: Environment Promotion
capabilities.description: Promote infrastructure configuration to higher environments
businessRules: Only forward promotion allowed (dev→sand→prod)
Configuration drift detection before promotion
Requires explicit approval number

capabilities.name: Infrastructure Discovery
capabilities.description: View all provisioned infrastructure and their status
businessRules: Metadata sourced from single source of truth
Age calculated dynamically from creation date
Status reflects current state from metadata

containerApplicationDeployment.description: Deploy containerized applications to managed Kubernetes clusters

capabilities.name: AKS Application Deployment
capabilities.description: Deploy containerized application to Azure Kubernetes Service
businessRules: Namespace must exist before deployment
Image must be in approved container registry
Resource limits are enforced

accessControlManagement.description: Manage access relationships between resources and identities

capabilities.name: RBAC Relationship Definition
capabilities.description: Define role-based access control between resources
businessRules: Resources must exist before relationship creation
Role assignments follow principle of least privilege
Cross-subscription relationships require additional approval
Roles loaded dynamically from external configuration via API endpoint
Role catalog served via GET /api/roles following module/template pattern
31+ roles across 10 scopes including App Configuration roles

workflowOrchestration.description: Coordinate infrastructure operations through automated workflows

capabilities.name: Workflow Triggering
capabilities.description: Initiate infrastructure workflow based on user action
businessRules: Each workflow instance has unique correlation ID
Workflow parameters validated before triggering
Authentication verified before workflow start
Authenticated user email (triggeredBy) captured and passed to all workflow types for audit trail
triggeredBy included in Pull Request descriptions for compliance tracking
Safe fallback: triggeredBy = req.user?.email || owner || 'unknown' prevents workflow failures

capabilities.name: Workflow Status Tracking
businessRules: Status queried via correlation ID
Multiple workflows can run concurrently
Status persisted for audit trail

capabilities.name: Approval Management
capabilities.description: Handle human approvals in workflow lifecycle
businessRules: High-risk operations require peer review
Approval requests tracked in version control
Auto-approval for low-risk operations

userInterface.description: Provide web-based interface for infrastructure operations

capabilities.name: Infrastructure Catalog Browsing
businessRules: Only display modules user has permission to deploy
Template descriptions loaded from catalog

capabilities.name: Form-Based Infrastructure Request
capabilities.description: Capture infrastructure requirements via structured forms
businessRules: All required fields must be provided
Validation happens client-side and server-side
Unique correlation ID generated on submission

capabilities.name: Real-Time Status Display
capabilities.description: Show workflow progress with polling mechanism
businessRules: Poll at regular intervals until completion
Display links to related resources (PRs, workflows)
Show errors with actionable guidance

capabilities.name: Infrastructure Inventory View
capabilities.description: Display all provisioned infrastructure with management actions
businessRules: Table sortable and filterable
Actions contextual based on infrastructure state
Age displayed in human-readable format

architecturalDecisions.description: Key design decisions independent of technology choices

AD001_GitOpsAsSourceOfTruth.decision: Use version control repository as primary data store for metadata
rationale: Built-in audit trail via git history
No separate database infrastructure to manage

cons: Limited query capabilities vs traditional database
Read performance scales with repository size

constraints: Write operations limited by git commit frequency

AD002_StatelessBackend.decision: Backend API servers maintain no session state
rationale: Enables horizontal scaling without sticky sessions

cons: Client must include context (correlation ID) in each request
No server-side caching of user state

constraints: All workflow tracking via correlation IDs
Client responsible for maintaining UI state

AD003_ClientSidePolling.decision: Client polls server for workflow status rather than webhooks or server-push

cons: Status updates delayed by polling interval

constraints: Polling interval configurable to balance responsiveness vs traffic
Backend must efficiently serve repeated status queries
Client must handle network failures gracefully

AD004_CorrelationIDTracking.decision: Unique correlation ID tracks each operation across all system layers
rationale: Link user actions to infrastructure changes
Support concurrent operations by same user
Audit trail from UI to infrastructure

cons: Must propagate through all system layers

constraints: Passed in all subsequent API calls

AD005_ApprovalViaVersionControl.decision: High-risk operations require approval via pull request review
rationale: Audit trail of who approved what

cons: Slower approval cycle than dedicated system
Requires reviewers familiar with version control
Cannot enforce approval by specific roles

constraints: PR must include operation details in description
Approver must have repository write access

cons: Some operations awkward in declarative model

constraints: State tracked in version control or state backend

AD007_MultiApplicationAuthentication.decision: Separate authentication contexts for different operation types

pros: Limited blast radius of credential compromise

constraints: Each context requires separate credential configuration
Must handle failure of individual auth contexts
Different contexts may have different rate limits

dataFlows.description: Key data flows through the system (technology-agnostic)

provisionInfrastructure.trigger: User submits custom infrastructure or template request

steps.data: projectName, environment, modules/template, owner, lifecycle, approvalNumber

substeps: Create pull request with code and metadata (after workflow execution)
steps.note: GitHub Actions workflow runs FIRST (60% progress), then creates PR (90% progress)

steps.action: Updates workflow status based on execution state

provisionInfrastructure.successOutcome: Infrastructure provisioned, metadata stored, user notified
provisionInfrastructure.failureOutcome: Error message shown to user, rollback initiated if needed

steps.action: Selects infrastructure to delete from inventory
Displays confirmation dialog with impact assessment

deleteInfrastructure.successOutcome: Infrastructure deleted, metadata archived, audit trail created
deleteInfrastructure.failureOutcome: Resources preserved, error logged, user notified

steps.action: Generates correlation ID at operation start
steps.persistence: Correlation ID stored with workflow metadata

steps.action: Begins polling status endpoint with correlation ID

steps.display: Progress bar, status text, action links

statusTracking.successOutcome: User sees real-time progress of operation
statusTracking.failureOutcome: Status unavailable message, retry mechanism engaged

scalability.requirement: Support increasing number of infrastructure requests

reliability.approach: Idempotent operations, retry logic, graceful degradation
metrics: Data loss tolerance: Zero for metadata
mechanisms: Metadata versioned in git prevents loss
Failed workflows can be manually restarted

security.requirement: Secure infrastructure operations with audit trail
security.approach: Least privilege, approval workflows, comprehensive logging

usability.requirement: Self-service interface accessible to technical teams
usability.approach: Form-based interaction, real-time feedback, clear error messages
goals: Helpful error messages with remediation steps

maintainability.requirement: System easy to modify and extend
maintainability.approach: Modular architecture, clear separation of concerns, comprehensive documentation

auditability.requirement: Complete trail of who did what when
auditability.approach: All changes tracked in version control, correlation IDs in logs
capabilities: Track request from UI to infrastructure change

migrationConsiderations.description: Guidance for technology stack changes without architectural redesign

srcV2Implementation.description: Vue 3 srcV2 implementation captures all architectural patterns with modern technology

auditTrail.pattern: Authenticated user email (triggeredBy) passed to all workflows
auditTrail.coverage: All 6 workflow types: custom, template, delete, promote, aks, label
auditTrail.visibility: Included in GitHub PR descriptions for compliance

dynamicConfiguration.pattern: External JSON configs (modules, templates, roles, agents) loaded via API
dynamicConfiguration.rationale: True dynamic loading enables external management without code changes

apiStandardization.pattern: All endpoints return {success, data, error, correlationId}

workflowSequence.pattern: GitHub Actions → Pull Request (not PR → Actions)

frontendFrameworkMigration.scenario: Replace vanilla JavaScript with modern framework (React, Vue, Angular)
frontendFrameworkMigration.status: IMPLEMENTED - Vue 3 with TypeScript in srcV2/
architecturalStability: Polling mechanism replaced with Vue composables (useWorkflowPolling)

implementation.routing: Custom navigation via stores/navigation.ts (future: Vue Router)
composables: useApi - Centralized API client with automatic auth token refresh

mappingGuidance.vanillaPages: Migrated to Vue page components with reactive state
mappingGuidance.vanillaFormValidation: Replaced with reactive form validation in components

developmentModes.hotReload: npm run dev:client (Vite on :5173, proxies /api to Express :3000)
developmentModes.production: npm run build:client → USE_VUE=true npm start

backendLanguageMigration.scenario: Replace Node.js with Go, Python, Java, etc.

architecturalStability: API contracts add auth header support
All operations still tracked via correlation ID
implementation: JWT Bearer tokens validated via middleware/auth.js
User identity extracted from req.user.email for all authenticated requests
User email captured as triggeredBy and passed to all 6 workflow types
Centralized API client (srcV2/services/api.ts) with automatic 401 token refresh
Public endpoints: GET /api/roles, GET /api/modules, GET /api/templates, GET /api/agents
workflowIntegration: All workflows receive triggeredBy parameter in inputs
GitHub Actions include triggeredBy in PR descriptions for audit trail
Workflow types: provision-custom, provision-template, delete, promote, deploy-aks, label-change

changes: Replace file-based storage with database queries
Keep git as audit trail, database as query optimization
